title: From Youth Learning Needs to AI-Supported SDG/ODA Education Design: Evidence from Ukraine and a Cross-National Benchmark
content: Education for Sustainable Development requires learning approaches that are accessible, context-sensitive, and responsive to learners’ actual needs. This study investigates the educational needs of Ukrainian youth regarding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Official Development Assistance (ODA) and examines how these needs can inform AI-supported educational design. A cross-national mixed-methods survey was conducted within the YouthSOFTPOWER project, involving 498 respondents (374 youth and 124 youth workers/educators). Ukraine served as the primary analytical case (n = 99), while respondents from other countries (n = 399) formed a pooled international benchmark. Quantitative analyses compared awareness, previous learning experience, willingness to participate in SDG/ODA education, learning barriers, and preferred learning formats. Open-ended responses were analyzed using LLM-assisted thematic coding followed by researcher validation. Ukrainian respondents demonstrated lower SDG awareness, less previous participation in SDG/ODA-related training, and lower willingness to engage in future learning than the international benchmark, whereas ODA awareness was low across both groups. Qualitative findings highlighted the need for plain language, authentic ODA case studies, concise visual materials, project-based learning, and interactive educational formats. These findings were translated into evidence-informed AI-supported design priorities that emphasize understandable explanations, localized case-based learning, microlearning, experiential learning, and interactive engagement. The study provides a human-centred framework for AI-supported SDG/ODA education grounded in empirically identified learner needs and researcher-validated evidence.
